thread:
Maya (oncall): Pager fired: billing-metering anomaly. We're seeing token counts drop into buckets with irregular granularity starting ~08:12 UTC. Overage flags triggered for a handful of customers. Paging SRE and Billing.
Raj (sre): looking. Can you paste last good vs current counters? rough idea of magnitude?
Kelly (billing): seeing alerts for customers cust_42, cust_78 — estimated overage ticks for 10-30min windows. No invoices yet but flags set. Holding comms until we know root cause.
Tom (infra): I'm tailing the aggregator logs. Noted a spike in streaming reconnects to ingest workers at 08:11. Could be partial duplicate suppression misfiring.
Maya (oncall): Incidents-bot created incident INC-2026-142. Priority P1 -> paging rotation engaged. @Raj @Tom pls coordinate. @Kelly we need customer impact summary asap.
incidents-bot: [AUTOMATION] Created INC-2026-142 | Incident channel: #incident-1769991234 | Runbook: metering-aggregation
Raj (sre): quick check: run this on the aggregation leader: `curl -s http://agg-leader:9100/metrics | grep token_counter` then compare to raw ingest logs from the kafka partition. I see counters have uneven increments (mostly jumps of 2500 tokens instead of 1000).
Tom (infra): pulling kafka consumer lag and offsets now. Looks like aggregator batching window changed from 1s to 3s on a single node after a config restart. That explains bigger jumps and misaligned bucketing.
Kelly (billing): If the batch window increased, billing counts would be coarser. Customers get flagged for overages if their short-window rates exceed thresholds. Which customers hit rolling thresholds vs bucket misalignment?
Sophia (prod-sup): Customer impact: cust_42 reported spike via support ticket at 08:20, they see internal alerts. cust_78 opened chat but no official support ticket yet. Both are on dedicated capacity but still rely on server-side metering for billing assertions.
Maya (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) revert aggregator window config to 1s on the effected node 2) toggle graceful backfill so we don't double-count while offsets catch up 3) instruct billing to mute automated overage emails for the 08:10-08:30 window until recon.
Raj (sre): Rolling revert now to agg-node-3. Patch command: `ssh agg-node-3 'sudo systemctl edit --full aggregator; set BATCH_WINDOW=1s; systemctl restart aggregator'` Doing it.
Tom (infra): Confirming consumer offsets are stable. Kinesis->kafka adapter had a tls handshake glitch during the restart cascade. Toggling adapter retry backoff to default and restarting will reduce bursty recons.
incidents-bot: [ACTION] agg-node-3 restart - initiated by Raj at 08:24:12 UTC
Raj (sre): agg-node-3 back to steady state. token_counter increments back to ~1k per step in metrics. Patching script to force consistent batch window across nodes to avoid config drift.
Kelly (billing): On hold for muting emails. I've paused overage notifications for billing-alerts group and flagged the 08:10-08:30 window for manual review. Will open a recon ticket for adjustments to any automated credits if customers billed.
Sophia (prod-sup): Notifying cust_42 that we're investigating and may issue adjustments if counts were affected. Short message drafted: "We've identified a transient metering aggregation issue between 08:10-08:30 UTC that may have produced inaccurate usage flags. We're rolling fixes and will follow up with reconciled usage within 2 hours." Ready to send once you confirm.
Maya (oncall): Confirmed. Send to cust_42 & cust_78. Add temporary slack contact channel for them if needed.
Tom (infra): Starting post-mortem checklist: capture config drift root cause, add guard in deploy pipeline to validate batch window consistency, add metric alert for sudden change in batch size distribution (histogram shift).
Raj (sre): Also adding a short-term mitigation: emit synthetic per-request tokens before batch commit so billing can read a smoother per-second rate when aggregator is uncertain. Will spike latency <5ms but safe.
Kelly (billing): We'll run the recon job against raw ingest logs to recompute token-level billing for the window. ETA 90 minutes for initial report. If recon shows inflated counts, we'll auto-apply adjustments and roll back overage flags.
Sophia (prod-sup): Sent updates to customers. No angry emails yet, just FYI pings. They appreciate the transparency.
Maya (oncall): Good. Handoff to Raj for post-restart monitoring and to Kelly for billing recon. I'll stay on for 30 more minutes then hand to next oncall @Raj.
Raj (sre): Monitoring dashboards show stable behavior. No additional overage flags since 08:28. I'll stay on watch and run the recon verification when billing finishes.
Kelly (billing): Recon started. I will post results in this thread when done and notify finance ops if adjustments needed.
incidents-bot: [INCIDENT UPDATE] INC-2026-142 -> status: mitigated (root cause in progress) at 08:35 UTC
Maya (oncall): Closing immediate pager. Keep thread active for recon notes. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Tom (infra): filing follow-up: `PM-1769991234` with action items (deploy guard, adapter retry tuning, monitoring). Linking here once created.
Kelly (billing): Recon summary: raw ingest shows token sequence aligned to actual requests; aggregator batched larger windows for 18 min due to config drift, resulting in coarse bucket increments that triggered rate-based overage heuristics for 6 customers. Proposed remediation: apply reconciled usage (dedupe batch gap) and revoke automated overage labels. I'll attach CSV when ready.
Raj (sre): Thanks. Let's run the reconciliation and schedule a postmortem doc in 24h. Also add a synthetic test in staging to simulate node restarts with config refresh.
Maya (oncall): Noted. Last update here and then I'll archive and add to postmortem list.
